assets.prompt_structure: Reference-role preamble (@Image1/@Image2) + timestamped action-block timeline (6 beats) + inline continuity constraints + closing dash negative-prompt line. No separate validation clip run first, per the 2026-09-20 process correction.
assets.approval_note: Tony: approved, grade C. Technically clean (scooter arrives/delivers/departs, tanuki emerges at correct scale, natural camera reaction, real physical tell before retreat) but narratively flat -- 'wasn't that great,' just sequential passive observation with no interaction or gag. Root cause identified as the matrix cell/story premise, not execution quality.

issues.note: Story/premise issue, not a technical defect: the arrive-notice-watch-leave structure has no built-in comedic engine. Worked better on Shot 02 (kangaroo) where the animal itself carried the scene; failed here because a tanuki quietly retreating isn't inherently funny. Future matrix cells need an explicit, deliberately chosen comedic hook (interaction, mimicry, misunderstanding, behavioral gag), not just axis variation.

Mid-2000s SD camcorder look still didn't render even with the aesthetic pushed directly into the video prompt -- likely a real Seedance limitation rather than a prompt-wording gap. Did not block approval.
